children: Rockwell Automation named Tessa Myers as its next chief revenue officer amid a number of other internal leadership changes.
Myers succeeds Scott Genereux, who plans to retire from Rockwell Automation at the end of 2026, the industrial automation and digital transformation company said Thursday.

Myers is currently Rockwell Automation's senior vice president, intelligent devices. She will be succeeded in that role by Matt Fordenwalt, who is currently senior vice president, lifecycle services. Fordenwalt joined the company in 2005.

Jordan Reynolds will take Fordenwalt's role leading the company's lifecycle services business segment. Reynolds joined Rockwell in 2020 and is currently vice president, artificial intelligence and autonomy.
The company said the changes will take effect Oct. 1.
